pr_title: Remove disposed security data from TimeSlice
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
If we pull data and on the same time step that security gets removed,
we can still get that data in OnData(Slice) even though it was removed.
This change filters out removed securities by tracking a reference to
the subscription's disposed flag. Another change was made to wait until
the end of the time step to dispose of subscriptions.

issue_context.title: Data for recently removed securities shows up in OnData
issue_context.body:
In the time step that universe selection occurs, it is possible to get data for securities that were just removed via universe selection. This is due to sometimes synchronizing the data before the universe selection logic has been applied, so we've already dequeued the data.

See https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/pull/1444 for a proposed solution. Ideally, we could address this structurally, that is, perhaps by making universe selection always happen before we synchronize other data at that time step. This would preclude us from needing to manage extra state about pending removals and such.

review_comments: thanks! I don't think we use it as keys to a dictionary anymore, but we used to, wonder what kind of weird things happened as a result! I went to use it in a `HashSet<T>` and was like, hmm, maybe double check equals/gethashcode
Does this ever get hit now?

This gets hit during universe selection algorithms. The algorithm listed above on current `master` has some time steps that emit data for 60 securities instead of 50. After this change, each time step emits data for 50 securities as expected. The underlying cause was enumerating the data feed subscription before performing universe selection. I had considered using sorting to enforce an order to the enumeration but felt this required less coupling/coordination between data feed and universe selection mechanics.

`Ref` is a custom type created to allow us to pass references to value types. A more common implementation is `Box<T>` which would maintain it's own storage. `Ref<T>` is defined in such a way that it doesn't maintain it's own storage and instead uses functions to get/set a value. Originally written to enable a shared fill forward increment, as the fill forward time span is maintained by the data feeds but required in all enumerator stacks and potentially updated each time a subscription is added or removed from the feed.
